# New house-rendering proposals — odyssey-010 (Odyssey 3.102–209)

Formulas, epithets and proper names that recur (or plausibly will recur) beyond this part and are
not yet fixed in `conventions.md`'s house table.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἀρήιος (109, 167) | "warlike" | "warlike" | "war-loving", "martial" (too Latinate) |
| ἀτάσθαλα (207, adj./subst., distinct lemma from the already-fixed noun ἀτασθαλίαι) | "wanton deeds" / "wanton things" | "wanton deeds" | "reckless", "outrageous acts" — kept to echo the fixed ἀτασθαλίαι "wanton-follies" |
| λυγρός (132 λυγρὸν νόστον, 194 λυγρὸν ὄλεθρον) | "grievous" | "grievous" | "baneful", "woeful", "miserable" |
| θεσπέσιος of a sound (150 ἠχῇ θεσπεσίῃ; cf. the already-fixed θεσπεσίην … χάριν) | "wondrous" | "wondrous" | "divine", "prodigious", "supernatural" |
| Ἀτρεΐδῃ Ἀγαμέμνονι (156, 164; cf. Ἀτρεΐδῃσι 136, Ἀτρεΐδην alone 193) | "Atreus' son Agamemnon" | "Agamemnon, son of Atreus" | "the son of Atreus" alone when the name Agamemnon is also given |
| Ἀτρεΐδης / Ἀτρεΐδην used alone as a name-substitute (193) | "the son of Atreus" | "the son of Atreus" | naming him "Agamemnon" outright where the Greek withholds the name |
| Τυδέος υἱός / Τυδεΐδης (periphrasis and patronymic for Diomedes) | "the son of Tydeus" | "the son of Tydeus" | naming him "Diomedes" where the Greek uses the periphrasis alone |
| ἱππόδαμος applied to a figure other than Nestor (181, of Diomedes) | "horse-taming" | "tamer of horses" | keeps the wording already fixed for Νέστωρ ἱππόδαμος, now reused for its plain adjectival sense |
| μεγάθυμος (189, of Achilles) | "great-hearted" | "great-hearted" | "great-souled", "high-spirited" |
| φαίδιμος (189, "φαίδιμος υἱός") | "glorious" | "glorious" | "shining", "splendid" (reserved for ἀγλαός) |
| ἀγλαός (190, "Ποιάντιον ἀγλαὸν υἱόν") | "splendid" | "splendid" | "glorious" (reserved for φαίδιμος), "radiant" |
| ποιμένι λαῶν ("shepherd of the people", 156) | "shepherd of the people" | "shepherd of the people" | "shepherd of hosts", "leader of men" |

## Flagged for the reviewer

- **3.103–108 and 3.168–172 and 3.180–182 comma-cuts**: several sentences ran past the four-line
  limit with no intervening ano teleia/question mark/full stop, so I cut at the comma where the
  syntax paused most (e.g. after Ἀχαιῶν at 104, after ὁρμαίνοντας at 169). These are judgment calls
  about which comma is the strongest pause; a reviewer may prefer a different split point.
- **3.135, 3.202**: γλαυκώπιδος ὀβριμοπάτρης (135) and κεῖνος (196, 202, referring to Orestes) never
  name Athena or Orestes outright in this stretch. I kept the periphrasis/pronoun literal rather than
  inserting the names for clarity — consistent with how the table already treats other unnamed
  periphrases (e.g. ἱερὴ ἲς Τηλεμάχοιο), but a reviewer may want the note to say more.
- **3.199–200 (packet text vs. the "already published" quote)**: the packet's own line-listing gives
  this line as "καὶ σὺ φίλος, μάλα γάρ …" (no comma after σύ), while the packet's "already published"
  section quotes it as "καὶ σύ, φίλος, μάλα γάρ …" (comma after σύ, acute accent). I cut `t` exactly
  as the packet's line-listing prints it, but reused the published `l`/`i` verbatim as instructed,
  since this is unmistakably the same verse (3.200). Flagging the discrepancy between the packet's
  two transcriptions in case it needs correcting upstream.
- **ἐπισμυγερῶς (195)**: a rare adverb, translated "most grievously" / "a bitter penalty"; I did not
  find it fixed anywhere in the table and did not add it there, judging it unlikely to recur often,
  but a reviewer with a fuller concordance view may disagree.
- **3.209, end of Telemachus's speech**: "νῦν δὲ χρὴ τετλάμεν ἔμπης." ends with a full stop and is a
  grammatically complete, self-contained clause (χρή + infinitive, no open construction), so I judged
  the thought complete at 3.209 and said so in that unit's note. The speech itself likely continues
  as direct discourse in odyssey-011 (Nestor replying again), but the sentence at 3.209 is not left
  hanging.
